text:
lia: Pushing an RFC follow-up idea  Precision Tier Selector. Instead of a single global quant rollout, we expose per-tenant "tier" rules that map traffic to FP8/INT8/4bit lanes based on heuristics (prompt length, latency sensitivity tag, and customer SLA).

jon: interesting. so routing decisions are upstream at the selector service, not per-request model negotiation?

lia: yep. selector returns a lane id and a quant_profile_id. runtime consumes quant_profile_id only. avoids expensive handshakes in hot path.

priya: how are lanes defined? static buckets or dynamic scoring? we should support both. e.g., static for enterprise customers with contracts, dynamic for opportunistic batching.

lia: propose a dual model: static tiers (gold/silver/beta) that can be pinned per-customer, plus an adaptive scorer that nudges individual requests into lower-precision lanes when they are short prompts and cache-friendly.

dan: developer question: what metrics govern adaptive scoring? simple features: token_count < 64, kv_cache_hit=true, prompt_entropy < threshold. combined into a score and a threshold per-lane.

jon: what about quality checks? we need an online signal to catch quality drift quickly. degscore alone is noisy.

priya: we can maintain small per-lane shadow evals: for each lane, sample x responses per minute, compute embedding distance vs FP32 baseline and a classification hallucination score. if either exceeds thresholds we demote the lane for affected tenants.

lia: agree. add a cohort-based alarm: if 3+ tenants in the same region show drift within a rolling 30m window, treat it as model-level issue and pause all dynamic promotions.

dan: cache implications: we must namespace KV and attention caches by quant_profile_id. also consider incremental cache migration for long sessions. migrating is risky because encoding differs across quant.

jon: session pinning then? sessions created under a lane get a "precision_affinity" flag. if pinned, selector won't move subsequent requests. we'll surface a warning in the SDK when switching.

priya: billing for shadow evals is a question. should token cost come from tenant quota or platform?

lia: baseline plan: platform pays for up to N shadow tokens per tenant per month; anything above is billable/on opt-in. we'll show expected overhead in the Console's Billing tab.

deploy-bot: canary-run: precision-tier-selector prototype deployed to staging. 1000 simulated requests, lanes: FP8=15%, INT8=30%, 4bit=5% (rest fp32). embedding-drift stats: fp8 median=0.018, int8 median=0.027, 4bit median=0.055.

dan: 4bit drift 0.055 looks high. what's our cutoff? previously we used 0.05.

lia: update: new policy uses asymmetric thresholds: lanes can have different tolerances based on SLA. by default 4bit threshold=0.06 for prob tasks, 0.04 for precision tasks. we'll attach task-sensitivity labels to endpoints.

jon: ops concern: rolling back lanes should be fast and safe. plan: selector can toggle a lane boolean (enabled/disabled) per-tenant and globally. routing uses a cached config with TTL=5s so changes propagate quickly.

priya: we need observability: per-tenant time series for embedding drift, golden prompt regression, hallucination rate, latency p99, kv-cache-hit. also a composite "quality_score".

lia: agreed. add a daily snapshot to help model teams correlate training changes with lane regressions.

dan: one more edge: mixed-precision multi-request sessions (one request in session used fp8, next used fp32) could produce inconsistent outputs due to KV mismatch. We'll disallow mixed precision inside pinned sessions.

jon: let's capture the minimal profile schema for the selector, JSON example: 

```json
{
  "tenant": "beta-corp",
  "static_tier": "silver",
  "adaptive": {
    "enabled": true,
    "rules": [
      {"feature": "token_count", "op": "<", "value": 64, "weight": 0.4},
      {"feature": "kv_cache_hit", "op": "==", "value": true, "weight": 0.4},
      {"feature": "prompt_safety_score", "op": ">", "value": 0.9, "weight": 0.2}
    ],
    "thresholds": {"fp8": 0.7, "int8": 0.5, "4bit": 0.9}
  },
  "pinned_sessions_allowed": false,
  "fallbacks": ["int8","fp32"],
  "billing": {"shadow_tokens_free": 10000}
}
```

priya: looks good. ensure schema has versioning (schema_v) so migrations are manageable.

lia: will add schema_v and an encoded quant_profile_id. also need tests for selector determinism (same inputs -> same lane for TTL window).

deploy-bot: perf-check: selector adds ~0.3ms median overhead in staging. caching cut that to ~0.05ms after warmup.

dan: small but acceptable. automation: we should include offline regression harness that replays production traces and measures lane-level deltas before any model or kernel changes get rolled out.

jon: next steps: write RFC addendum with schema_v and rollout playbook, prototype selector service, run replay tests on top 20 tenants, and add console UX for lane visibility + one-click revert.

lia: I'll open the addendum PR and a JIRA for the prototype. tagging @platform for routing TTL concerns and @console for UI backlog. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
